concerns.text: User Story US2 (Linguistic Feature Extraction and Statistical Testing) has no associated functional requirement (FR) in the Functional Requirements section, leaving its implementation under‑specified.
User Story US3 (Predictive Modeling and Validation) has no associated functional requirement (FR) in the Functional Requirements section, so its scope is not anchored to any concrete requirement.
The specification does not contain a Success Criteria section (SC‑### IDs). Consequently none of the user stories have measurable acceptance criteria, violating the requirement‑coverage rule.

Duplicate functional requirement identifier FR-001 appears in the Spec Template section as a placeholder, conflicting with the earlier concrete FR-001 defined in the Functional Requirements section. This creates ambiguity about which FR-001 is authoritative.
The inclusion of a generic 'Spec Template' with placeholder requirements (e.g., FR-001‑006) is inappropriate for a finalized specification document and introduces redundant terminology and IDs.

Performance requirement states “pipeline must complete within 6 hours on a standard CPU environment” but does not define the hardware profile (CPU model, core count, RAM) nor a reproducible measurement procedure, making the criterion unmeasurable.
Memory requirement says “Peak RAM usage must not exceed a moderate threshold” without specifying a concrete numeric limit or how the measurement should be taken, so it cannot be verified.

Privacy requirement “No PII should be logged or stored; transcripts must be anonymized” lacks a definition of what constitutes PII and does not describe an observable check (e.g., schema validation, regex audit), rendering it unverifiable.

The specification contains no Success Criteria (SC‑xxx) section. Without explicit, measurable SC IDs (e.g., SC‑001: “p50 end‑to‑end pipeline latency ≤ X seconds on hardware Y”), there is no way to assess whether the project meets its goals.

FR‑001 describes edge‑case handling (missing labels, insufficient length) but does not state the observable outcome (e.g., “records with missing labels are omitted from the output CSV”) – adding the expected output artifact state would make the requirement directly verifiable.

User Story US3 adds predictive modeling (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, nested k‑fold CV) which was not part of the original research idea. The idea only required statistical association analysis, not supervised prediction, so this extends the scope beyond what was requested.

The performance constraint ('pipeline must complete within 6 hours on a standard CPU') and memory limit are engineering limits not mentioned in the original idea. While reasonable, they constitute additional scope that was not requested and may restrict implementation choices unnecessarily.

The specification calls for Mann‑Whitney U tests (a non‑parametric test) and then requests reporting effect sizes as Cohen's d (a parametric measure). Cohen's d assumes normally distributed data and is not appropriate for rank‑based tests; a more suitable non‑parametric effect size (e.g., rank‑biserial correlation) should be used.

Mean AUC is reported as the primary performance metric, but the task involves three diagnostic groups (Control, MCI, AD). AUC is defined for binary classification; the spec does not specify how multi‑class AUC will be computed (e.g., one‑vs‑rest, macro‑averaged). This ambiguity makes the validation method ill‑defined.

The analysis does not account for known confounding variables (e.g., age, education level) that influence both language use and cognitive status. Without adjusting for these covariates, any observed linguistic differences may be spurious, threatening the validity of the claimed relationship between linguistic markers and cognitive decline.

new_concerns.text: Functional Requirement FR-005 (Privacy & Data Anonymization) is not anchored to any User Story or stated project goal; it only references the Non‑Functional Requirements section, leaving its scope unbacked by a concrete story.

Success Criterion SC-002 demands ≥ 1000 records after exclusions, but the ADReSS dataset contains far fewer recordings (≈ 300). This creates an unattainable requirement, contradicting the defined data source scope.

SC-002 mandates that the cleaned dataset contain ≥ 1000 records after exclusions. The ADReSS dataset contains far fewer records (≈ 300), so this threshold is unreachable under the defined scope, rendering the success criterion untestable.

Success Criterion SC-002 requires the cleaned dataset to contain ≥ 1000 records after exclusions, but the ADReSS dataset comprises only ~156 participants. This makes the criterion infeasible given the declared data source, risking forced data augmentation or unrealistic expectations and thus undermining the study’s methodological validity.
